physicalNotes: Radius 0.20608475 Jupiter radii from Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract): 14,733.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0393294 Jupiter masses (Howard et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..278...52H/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): P 14.09292 d
sources.shape: Howard et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..278...52H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HOWARD_ET_AL__2025): a/R* derived by Kepler's third law from its period 14.09292 d, stellar mass 0.84 and radius 0.809 solar units; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 89.16344 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Kruse et al. 2019 (2019ApJS..244...11K), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname KRUSE_ET_AL__2019): transit mid-time 2456907.2322 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 211 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
